VERDICT goal: the node goal is to measure what a node's time budget controls and how much of it the gates spend; docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:26-39 answers the first half with a deadline-path table whose every cited line I resolved in the reviewed tree, and :105-109 answers the second with a per-lane gate-share table.
VERDICT done_when: the done_when's table columns, by-id lists, resolved watchdog fence and both positive controls are present, and the figures reconcile with the stored payload: out/gate-share.json gives clive 737 runs / 7.16% over 143 / 8.35% over 292 / fallback 0.431 and codex 164 / 7.89 over 47 / 7.89 over 49 / 0.024, and out/fences.json holds 18 projects all resolving false.
VERDICT write_paths: the manifest declares docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html, scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py, the landing fragment and a figures directory; git diff --stat c941de7658..916b9c8c48 lists exactly the first three, and the figures directory is unused.
VERDICT manifest: read /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261103T072523194588-measure-what-a-nodes-time-budget-controls-and-how-much-of-it/manifest.md; it states status complete, tests: none, negative_control_log: none, and its 901-run, 560-unmeasurable and 146-truncated figures reconcile with the payload at out/gate-share.json.
VERDICT diff: read both commits against base c941de7658 - 5dbf6b0455 adds the research document (134 lines) and the script (499 lines), 916b9c8c48 adds the 49-line fragment, 682 insertions and no other file.
CALL_SITES: none
SCORE goal_fidelity: 17
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:35 names _apply_budget_watchdog as the only acting path and :52 resolves the fence false for all 18 mounted projects, which is the goal's first half, while :107 carries the second half's per-lane share.
SCORE evidence: 15
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the document's figures reproduce exactly from out/gate-share.json and its 543.02 s control reproduces when re-run, but scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:155 cannot read any codex stream so the codex fallback and background zeros rest on an unstated structural limit, and docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:67 names a command for only one of the three figures groups.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: git diff --stat c941de7658..916b9c8c48 changes only docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html, scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py and the landing fragment, all inside the four declared paths.
SCORE durability: 4
JUSTIFICATION durability: no test covers scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py and the node is suite-unarmed, so nothing reddens if the join or the median regresses; the only check is the one-shot control at docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:96, which compares the scanner's read of gate-after.log with that same log's text and therefore cannot fail on a duration error.
SCORE fit: 8
JUSTIFICATION fit: scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:1 is a new file that adds seven ruff findings and fails ruff format --check at the 0.16.4 the lock pins, against reckon/AGENTS.md's rule that a commit adds no findings; its names and structure otherwise follow the surrounding scripts.
SCORE reuse: 5
JUSTIFICATION reuse: scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:239 re-implements reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:508 _recorded_gate_seconds and drops its preserved-log fallback, and :155 re-reads streams beside reckon/shadow_reads.py:66 stream_tool_calls, which already owns both dialects; the module docstring at :17-22 claims both owners as reused.
FINDING scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:1 blocking: the new file adds seven ruff findings (EXE001, UP035, FURB162, RUF021, SIM114, PERF401, W292) and fails ruff format --check under ruff 0.16.4, the version uv.lock pins, so the commit adds findings where reckon/AGENTS.md requires none; it also carries an unused module constant _TRUNCATION_FLAGS at :48 that nothing reads.
FINDING scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:239 non-blocking: _log_seconds re-implements reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:508 _recorded_gate_seconds - same read, same _GATE_LOG_DURATION.findall, same last-match float - and drops the owner's preserved-log fallback, so a gate whose worktree log was released reports unmeasurable where the owner would still find a duration.
FINDING scripts/gate_share_of_run_time.py:155 non-blocking: _bash_calls_with_timing parses only the message/content dialect, so it returns zero calls on every codex stream (measured: r-20261020T112748325543 gives 100 bash calls through reckon/shadow_reads.py:66 and 0 here, r-20261103T064034359291 gives 134 and 0); codex item events carry no timestamp key at all, so the codex lane is structurally unable to yield a tool-call gate, and docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:120-130 never says so, leaving the codex fallback and background zeros readable as observations.
FINDING docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:62 non-blocking: the stated measurement instant 2026-11-03T07:56:55Z is the scan's completion time while the corpus window ends at 07:51:45, the since and until stamps in the payload it cites, so a reader cannot tell which instant the counts belong to.
FINDING docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:67 non-blocking: the command given is said to produce every figure below, but the section 1 fence table comes from --fences (out/fences.json) and the section 3 control from --control-run, and neither invocation is named anywhere, though the done_when requires the command for every figure.
FINDING docs/evidence/fragments/test-time-is-not-the-nodes-time/measure-what-a-nodes-time-budget-controls-and-how-much-of-it.html:34 non-blocking: the fragment states the window as the 14 days to 2026-11-03T08:58Z, but the payload records read_at 07:56:55.586892+00:00 and a window ending 07:51:45; 08:58 is a local (UTC+1) clock reading of a file write stamped as Z, a 61-minute overstatement of the window end.
FINDING docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:96 non-blocking: the timing control is not independent of the value under test - it compares the scanner's read of gate-after.log with that same log's own text, so it proves the join found the file, not that the duration extraction is right; a control that could fail would compare that log's duration with the foreground tool-call span of the same gate.
FINDING docs/research/how-much-of-a-node-is-its-gate.html:32 non-blocking: two citations in the file-and-line table resolve one line off the construct they name - prompts.py:502 is the docstring of _continuation_multiple whose def is at :501, and the watchdog call cited at dispatch_sessions.py:337 is on the blank line before the call at :338.
